pr_title: release-22.1: sql: better instruction for creating HSI in mixed version cluster
pr_body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #83521.
Fixes #83447

/cc @cockroachdb/release

---

Previously, we threw out an error indicating virtual columns not allowed in
primary key when creating hash sharded index in mixed version cluster with
upgrading from pre-22.1. With this commit, we will return better instructions
with options of what to do insteading confusing them with validation errors.
We still keep the validation as the last line of guard.

Note that, we won't prevent user from doing the work around in which a stored
shard column is created manually.

Release justification: There was a support issue where user got confused by
the insufficient validation error message. This commit adds more helpful
instructions to better educate users what is happening.

Release note (sql change): Previously, we simply threw a descriptor validation
error when a user tries to create hash sharded index in a mixed version cluster
upgrading from pre-22.1, which is confusing to user. Now, we return a message
instructing users to run the statement from a pre-22.1 node before the upgrade
is finalized or just wait until the upgrade is finalied.

issue_context.title: sql: bad version-gating of new hash-sharded behaviour
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Although we have been careful to version-gate the hash-sharding implementation in 22.1, it appears there's still at least one mixed-version cluster bug.

**To Reproduce**

```
$ roachprod create $CLUSTER -n 3
$ roachprod stage $CLUSTER release v21.2.10
$ roachprod sql $CLUSTER:1
```
At which point we disable auto-upgrades:
```
root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> SET CLUSTER SETTING cluster.preserve_downgrade_option = '21.2';
```
Now lets replace all the binaries:
```
$ roachprod stage $CLUSTER release v22.1.2
$ roachprod stop $CLUSTER:3
$ roachprod start $CLUSTER:3
$ roachprod stop $CLUSTER:2
$ roachprod start $CLUSTER:2
$ roachprod stop $CLUSTER:1
$ roachprod start $CLUSTER:1
```
I checked that the cluster version was still 21.2 and tried to create a hash-sharded index:
```
$ roachprod sql $CLUSTER:1
root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> SHOW CLUSTER SETTINGS;
...
  version                                                                   | 21.2                                                               | m            | set the active cluster version in the format '<major>.<minor>'
(206 rows)


Time: 11ms total (execution 3ms / network 8ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> CREATE TABLE kv (k INT PRIMARY KEY, v STRING);                 
CREATE TABLE


Time: 11ms total (execution 11ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> ALTER TABLE kv ALTER PRIMARY KEY USING COLUMNS (k) USING HASH WITH BUCKET_COUNT = 8;
ERROR: relation "kv" (52): primary index column "crdb_internal_k_shard_8" cannot be virtual
```

**Expected behavior**
The ALTER PRIMARY KEY statement should not fail with a validation error. (edited)

Jira issue: CRDB-17074
comments: should we close this since we disallow the creation of hash sharded index in mixed version version cluster on purpose and the customer was happy with creating it after finalizing the cluster upgrade?
I don't know, I don't think the behaviour I described in the repro is reasonable.

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/c54f99d6a144e237f4226c93266caafb4fddb705/pkg/sql/create_table.go#L2697 here's where we set the column to virtual.

I think we need to gate this behavior on the cluster version. In the mixed version state, we need to use a physical column
